fairness_rules: Separate source conservation, grammar/typing coherence, whole-content information and semantic selection.
Treat C0 glossary/reference/default hypotheses as permitted; reject concrete underdefinition or contradiction rather than requiring previously confirmed words.
Audit each model under its frozen rules and all59 IT groups before comparing narratives. Conditional alternate-reader compatibility does not make a consensus confirmation.
A nominated consumer signature is an authored cost. Its successful type check is internal coherence, not independent evidence for its English value or output ontology.
Permit paid typed overloads/coercions/quotation/invocation in either model when frozen in advance. Do not grant free bridges or prohibit a hybrid merely because it weakens contrast.

symmetries.name: Endpoint renaming
symmetries.invariance: Global A↔B leaves reciprocity, return feasibility and constructor relations unchanged. No literal A/B name, left/right vessel ownership or direction follows.

symmetries.name: Direction convention
symmetries.invariance: Reverse all edge orientations together with source/destination conventions and reference grammar. Bare ending covariance cannot select the English orientation; a local one-word swap inside a fixed grammar is a different intervention.

symmetries.name: Domain relabeling
symmetries.invariance: Opaque nodes can denote places, roles, accounts or other endpoints while retaining the same graph. Any historical/fluid description must be a separately paid semantic assumption.

symmetries.name: Relation/event reification
symmetries.invariance: An event can carry a named underlying relation; a relation can denote an allowed transition. Projection of a history to its traversed edges erases order/multiplicity. Equal projected graphs do not mean identical full histories.

symmetries.name: Latent repeatedness
symmetries.invariance: Round-trip once and repeated round-trips end at the same location; union is idempotent whereas event counts may differ. Counts/order matter only if an unchanged written construction actually asserts or refers to them.

symmetries.name: Static assertion of an event history
symmetries.invariance: Descriptive sentence mood can describe ordered events. Static versus imperative speech act is a separate axis from relation-set versus event-sequence denotation.

hybrid.definition: Let E={(B,A)} and R=E union converse(E). A named record R contains both directions. A separately licensed Invoke(R,participant,start=B,route=[B,A,B]) executes two ordered traversals and returns that participant to B. Queries may inspect R membership or the resulting history, using the specified object rather than a silent cast.

consequences.set_projection: the same edge set as R

participant and start binding/default if not written

hybrid.fair_cost_comparison: Incremental cost depends on the base model. An event author already naming relations does not pay a second copy of that facility; a static author adding execution must pay it. No fixed primitive count or probability is inferred.
hybrid.limitation: This abstract rival is not asserted to parse any target word. It cannot donate a consumer/start/participant to either frozen author. If no written invocation or ordering is authored, the event consequence is not derived.

counterfactual_audit.question: Does order carry information?
counterfactual_audit.operation: Compare two histories with identical traversed-edge sets but opposite first traversal or different multiplicity, keeping endpoints and lexical rules fixed.
counterfactual_audit.success: Identify which actual frozen written clause/reference changes truth or loses its required antecedent. If none changes, the continuation does not discriminate order.

counterfactual_audit.question: Does relation union carry information?
counterfactual_audit.operation: Compare a reciprocal relation with the same endpoint domain but only one of its two directed edges, without inventing new target words.
counterfactual_audit.success: Show an actual clause that rules out the one-edge interpretation. A self-equality or existence assertion is insufficient.

counterfactual_audit.question: Is the participant shared?
counterfactual_audit.operation: Replace the participant of the second traversal with a distinct instance while retaining the first participant and endpoint names.
counterfactual_audit.success: Show the unchanged written reference rule forbids the replacement. A same-spelling kind term or a critic-demanded same portion is insufficient.

counterfactual_audit.question: Is .41 sheolo necessary?
counterfactual_audit.operation: Delete only its authored contribution in the whole fixed model, preserving source provenance and no free fallback.
counterfactual_audit.success: Record exactly what derived relation/reference/history becomes unavailable. A985 B→A effect follows only if its premises are adopted; static/hybrid models have their own consequence.

counterfactual_audit.question: Are tail assertions informative?
counterfactual_audit.operation: State one alternative relation/history/participant configuration accepted by lexical inventory alone but excluded by the full frozen reading.
counterfactual_audit.success: Identify excluding source IDs/rules, including nonseed continuation. If all alternatives survive, full coverage is structurally/coherently rendered but not content-restricting.
